source_text: That's it is a good start, we can keep it up and keep working on it, though I'd rather rename it as daxiang_live so that Brendan isn't offended if we get something wrong and put his name on it (we should, however, add citations for any of his work that we use, see below).  It would be nice to have a few diagrams showing how itents flow through a system, and also to include a workup on the pattern cascade like we were working on.  It is WIP and this is the right place for it, as I am strictly about doing open research these days.   I'll ask Fable for some initial comments/revisions and we can maybe start to plan out a deep research task to create E-the-dark-tower-3.md as a source for working on this.  In terms of the format, this looks nice; we do have Clerk/Clay installed somewhere but we can leave it in this "minimal" format for now.  What I want to be sure of though is that we can actually extract/tangle the 大象 proper.  We could link to the notebook from https://hyperreal.enterprises/xiaoxiang.html and include there or on another page linked from index.html that 小象 is part of a broader family that reimplements the McCarthy Elephant-2000 ideas.  Again, we're in early stages of that so we don't need to go to town promising things we don't or can't deliver.  But what I'm seeing here is that this is actually a potentially quite good "product" that would allow people to get a lot more out of their LLMs.  I'm living in the future here in Emacs via rapid prototyping, and pretty soon we'll be able to port this to Element too.  But the power of the whole system will kick in when we connect 象 to custom memory systems.  Right now, what we're getting back from 大象 (who is the final elephant agent in the chain) goes into futon1b without much change.  But imagine that we had M-mark8 level semantic parsing going on, with intents flowing across a much bigger "evidence landscape" than just one person's chat history.  The *service* provision aspect is: we can build you a custom memory system that your agents can use.  That has to be a "service provision" because it is custom.  And it also has to be "we can build you" not just "we'll get Claude to bung it together overnight" because it's hard.

Now the renderer: raw-HTML values and a tangle step.Now the revised notebook, with 大象 as a tangled namespace, citations, diagrams and the cascade.㊥ (daxiang_live) Done. The notebook is now **大象 live**, at https://zone.hyperreal.enterprises/wip/notebooks/daxiang_live.html (the old fong_live page is gone). Fong and McCarthy are cited, not named in the title. 大象 itself is written in the notebook and tangled out to the source file the system runs, with a test that fails if the two drift. The page also has diagrams and the pattern cascade (`27f55cf0`).

㊢ (what changed)
- **Tangling.** 大象 proper, `futon3c.xiang.daxiang` (`read-agent-turn` and `asks-operator?`), is written in §2 of the notebook. `-m futon3c.notebook.render tangle notebooks/daxiang_live.clj` writes it to `src/futon3c/xiang/daxiang.clj`, which the JVM now loads. The token machine's "this turn ends by asking you" test now calls 大象, so there's one judge. 大象 also no longer counts a `🈸:` pointer (an answer to your 🈸) as a question.
- **Citations.** McCarthy's Elephant 2000 (Stanford 1992, revised 1998); Fong's *Causal Theories* (arXiv:1301.6201); *Decorated Cospans* (TAC 2015, arXiv:1502.00872). The page says mistakes in using them are ours. I left out the comb paper, because I couldn't verify its author.
- **Diagrams.** There are two, drawn as plain SVG (no layout engine is installed):
  - how intents flow from the turns through 小象 / 象 / 大象 into acts, the kernel, open ports, the reminder machine and futon1b;
  - the glued theory, coloured by which pattern owns each variable.
- **The cascade (§7–8).**
  - It's compiled from the library files: WR-26's `@why` cone, which is WR-26 → WR-8 and R20, then WR-8 → WR-0.
  - It uses one generic rule, taken from the library's own definition of `@why` ("a pattern's rationale is that it answers the problem this node states"). A pattern is unmet when its IF holds and its THEN doesn't. A problem counts as addressed when a pattern answering it holds.
  - It then runs on the real `象-off` switch from your log. The re-arm condition was written down ("Joe asks for 象 back") but isn't countable, so WR-26 and the cone above it come out unmet. A countable condition would have met all four.
  - The page states two cautions: other patterns outside this cone also answer those problems, and the countability test is only a first classical test.

㊬ (checked) The tangle test passes, as do 大象's question tests, including the `🈸:` pointer case. The reminder-machine suite still passes. The page renders 15 values and 3 figures, every one computed when the page was built.

㊢ (the 小象 page) I added one paragraph to the *staging* copy of xiaoxiang.html (`site-draft`, futon7 `c6626f1`). It names the Elephant 2000 family (小象 reads the person, 象 confirms, 大象 reads the agents), links the notebook, and says it's early research. The live site is unchanged until you say so.

㊭ (memory as a service) That framing seems right to me, and the work tonight shows why it can't be a quick build. Each piece only became useful once we tuned it to how you work:
- your mark conventions;
- what counts as a question to you;
- when waiting is legitimate.

A customer's memory system would need the same tuning against their own evidence landscape. That is service work, not packaging. When you plan E-the-dark-tower-3 with Fable, the notebook's §9 and this evening's fixes are concrete material for the "what's hard" section.

previous_reply_acts.text: (the ㊯ mark) Taken back. I delivered that paragraph, so it should have opened `㊯:`, which answers your ㊯. A bare ㊯ declares delegation. From now on, a paragraph that answers one of yours opens with your mark and a colon. That's also how 大象 and the reply-target code read it.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what the notebook shows, in order)
1. **The data.** Four consecutive turns from 1 October, copied unchanged. claude-17 asks you something you never answer, then offers two options. You answer "1", and a commit carries option 1 out.
2. **大象 reading the agent's reply.** Mark by mark, at 0.16 ms per reply, with no model involved.
3. **The session as acts.** The offer, your acceptance of it, and the commit that carries it out, linked only where the evidence is explicit.
4. **The marble run.** Open ports after each turn: the offer closes in turn 393, and the unanswered question from 391 is still open at the end.
5. **Three patterns as open theories.**
   - "answer your offers"
   - "the token machine"
   - "the operator's burden"

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(before you send it)
- **It's public.** The `wip/` area answers without a password, so the page is already reachable by anyone with the URL. It contains your words from those four turns, which are also in the repository and the turn feed.
- **The renderer is minimal.** It's a small renderer I wrote (`futon3c.notebook.render`): prose from `;;` comments, each code form evaluated in order, and its value shown. If you'd prefer a standard notebook format (Clerk or marimo), the content carries over.
- **The text should be checked.** The prose is mine. Read it for accuracy and tone before it goes to him, especially the opening paragraph and §7.
